This is a placeholder vignette showing the expected shape of an entry in the Vignettes listing: a short, self-contained exploration of one idea, question, or pattern in the data — not a full analysis or paper.
To add your own vignette:

Copy this file to a new name in vignettes/ (e.g. vignettes/dbh-vs-height.qmd).
Update the title, author, date, and description in the front matter above — these are what show up in the listing.
Replace this text with your own write-up. You can pull the underlying data from data/dataset.json, data/sector-summary.json, data/species-composition.json, or data/biomass-points.json (see the Sector Explorer source for examples of reading them with {ojs}), or from data/Placencia_mangroves_2025.xlsx directly in R or Python.

Keep it simple — a chart or two with a paragraph of interpretation is plenty.

title: Sampling Points
text: Each bubble marks a field station where trees were measured. Bubble size scales with the total biomass measured at that station; color matches the station’s lagoon sector (see the Sector Explorer for sector-level detail). Hover a bubble for its station id and totals.

Satellite Mapping
text: The lagoon sector boundaries shown on this site’s maps — upper, lower, and main creek — come from a mangrove extent polygon layer maintained separately from the field structural data, reflecting this project’s connection to the USF Institute for Marine Remote Sensing (IMaRS).

title: Satellite Mapping
section: From extent polygons to the site’s map
text:
From extent polygons to the site’s map
The source layer (data/placencia-sectors.geojson) contains 1,115 small mangrove-extent polygons, each tagged with a region. Before each site build, R/prepare_sector_map.R dissolves those polygons into the three named sectors and reprojects them from UTM zone 16N to WGS84 for the web map (data/placencia-sectors-map.geojson).

How the source extent polygons themselves were produced — imagery source, classification or digitization method, and validation — is maintained by the remote sensing team and not yet written up here. title: Mangrove Structure in Placencia
text:
Where to start

Sector Explorer — start here. Click a lagoon sector on the map to see its species mix, trunk diameter (DBH) and height distributions, and underlying tree-level data.
Sampling Points — a station-by-station view of total biomass sampled in the field.
Field Sampling and Satellite Mapping — background on how the field and mapping data were collected.
Vignettes — short, researcher-contributed explorations of the data.

title: Field Sampling
text: The structural dataset behind this site (Placencia_mangroves_2025.xlsx) is collected by hand in the field, tree by tree, across three lagoon sectors — upper, lower, and main creek — plus a handful of offshore caye sites not yet shown on the Sector Explorer map.

title: Field Sampling
text:
Data source
Field data are maintained in Placencia_mangroves_2025.xlsx on Google Drive. A local copy is fetched automatically before each site build; you can also download the spreadsheet directly.

title: Field Sampling
text:
What’s recorded per tree
For each sampled tree, the dataset records:

Location: a station id and, for the first tree at each station, latitude/longitude.
Species and morphotype (fringe vs. scrub growth form).
Trunk diameter (DBH) and height.
Lagoon position: upper/lower/main creek sector, and east/west bank.
Aboveground and belowground biomass per tree, calculated from the measurements above.

Trees are grouped by station, with a quarternumber and dist (distance) field indicating multiple trees measured outward from each station’s reference point — consistent with a transect- or quadrant-based sampling design radiating from fixed field stations.

title: Field Sampling
text:
Methodology
The specific field protocol (plot/transect layout, DBH measurement height, biomass allometric equations used, sampling dates, and personnel) is maintained by the field team and not yet written up here. This section is a placeholder — if you’re on the field team, replace it with the actual methodology, or open an issue/PR against the source repository.

title: Sector Explorer
text: Trees were sampled across three lagoon sectors — upper, lower, and main creek — plus a handful of offshore caye sites not yet shown on this map. Click a sector below to see its structure: species mix, trunk diameter (DBH) and height distributions, and the underlying tree-level data. To see biomass by individual field station instead, visit Sampling Points.
